issues.title: tools(art_review): shared bulk-select / mass-tag across all review sheets
issues.body:
## Summary

Pip's ask: "We don't seem to have the group select / mass add thing from one of the image set functions... uplift and ensure consistency for that functionality across galleries."

- Ported the bulk-select machinery (checkbox per cell, shift-click range select, select-all-visible, bulk apply/remove verdict bar) from `gen_contact_sheet.py` into `review_style.py` as shared `BULK_CSS` + additions inside the `VERDICT_JS` closure -- same pattern as the existing `COMPLETENESS_JS`/`COMPLETENESS_CSS`/`completeness_controls()` trio.
- It composes with the existing per-cell verdict chips, localStorage persistence, export/import JSON (flat `{rel: [tags]}` schema unchanged), and the three-state ALL / HIDE DECIDED / ONLY UNREVIEWED show control.
- Selection keys off `data-rel` (the README's compare-mode stable handle). Shift-click range select and "select all visible" both skip cells hidden by the current show-filter, so ONLY UNREVIEWED never silently pulls a filtered-out cell into a bulk action.
- **Automatic for every sheet that passes `verdict_key` to `page(...)`** -- no per-sheet wiring needed. That means `gen_prop_grain_sheet.py`, `build_worker_rebase_sheet.py`, `build_cat_sweep_sheet.py`, and `build_cat_refinement_sheet.py` all gain the feature on next regen with zero code changes of their own (checked: all four already build cells with `data-rel` + `rs-vtags` and call `rs.page(..., verdict_key=...)`).
- `gen_quirk_icon_sheet.py` (also `verdict_key`-driven) gains it too.
- `build_cat_angle_ab_sheet.py` has no `verdict_key` (pure comparison sheet, no verdict tags) so correctly gets the shared CSS but no bulk bar renders.
- `gen_contact_sheet.py` (the flagship sprite triage sheet, and the port source) is **left untouched** -- its own hand-rolled bulk-select differs enough (grid layout, run/category grouping, CSV export, copy-to-clipboard) that a safe migration needs the README's byte-diff verification pattern; not risked in this pass. Documented as a follow-up in the migration table.
- Updated `tools/art_review/README.md`: shared-house-style bullet list, "Sheets on the shared style" list (added the four newer builders, previously undocumented), migration status table, tracked/regenerable file lists, and a 2026-07-27 changelog note explaining the migration decision.

## Test plan

- [x] `python tools/art_review/review_style.py --selftest` passes
- [x] Regenerated all five affected sheets in the worktree: `gen_quirk_icon_sheet.py`, `gen_prop_grain_sheet.py`, `build_worker_rebase_sheet.py`, `build_cat_sweep_sheet.py`, `build_cat_refinement_sheet.py` -- all wrote successfully
- [x] Regenerated `build_cat_angle_ab_sheet.py` (no verdict_key) -- confirmed no `<div id="rs-bulkbar">` renders, only the (harmless, unused) shared CSS rules
- [x] Manually inspected emitted HTML/JS: checkbox creation, shift-click range logic (skips `display:none` cells), select-all-visible (filters on `style.display`), bulk apply/remove wiring, `.rs-selbox` / `.rs-bulkbar` CSS all present and correctly scoped
- [x] No non-ASCII characters introduced (checked both changed files)
- [x] `git status` after regenerating sheets shows only the two tracked source files modified -- all regenerated `art_generated/*.html` stay gitignored as expected

issues.title: fix(hiring): drain stranded pending_hire_queue back to the pool each turn (#952)
issues.body:
Fixes the verified half of #952.

## Bug

`queue_candidate_hire` (game_manager.gd:251) removes the candidate from `candidate_pool` the moment the hire is queued, but `execute_action` bails on the affordability check (actions.gd:231) BEFORE the `hire_*_researcher` arm calls `_hire_from_pool`. On that path the candidate was stuck in `pending_hire_queue` forever: not in the pool, never employed, invisible -- and the queue round-trips through saves, so the leak persisted.

Trigger in normal play: cash drops between queuing and execution (an earlier action in the same turn's execution order), so the hire fails and the candidate silently vanishes.

## Fix

New `_restore_stranded_hires` step at the end of `_step_execute_queued_actions`: hires only span a single turn's action step, so anyone still queued after it is stranded by definition -- return them to the pool, or narrate the walk-away in the results log if the pool refilled to cap (never a silent vanish). No RNG touched (stream-neutral); also self-heals stranded candidates in existing saves on their next turn.

## Tests

Two guard tests in `test_turn_manager.gd`: failed hire returns the candidate to the pool and employs nobody; full-pool edge drains the queue, respects the cap, and narrates the walk-away.

Fast gate: 801 tests, 0 failures, 85/85 files collected.

issues.title: CI: sim tier silently red on every main run -- test_adversarial_ui_state 6 deterministic invariant violations
issues.body:
## Summary
The non-blocking Simulation Tests job has FAILED on (at least) the last 5 main-branch runs (30183575511 .. 30192093124, 2026-07-25 23:56Z .. 2026-07-26 07:02Z), byte-identical each time: 6 tests in godot/tests/unit/simulation/test_adversarial_ui_state.gd (the #886 adversarial dialog fuzzer), deterministic (seed 727272), same violation counts to the digit. Totals per run: Scripts 8, Tests 106, Passing 100, Failing 6, Asserts 923/929.

Because the job is non-blocking, the red is invisible in the overall green -- the same failure pattern the honest-CI work (#640) was meant to prevent, one tier up.

## The 6 failing tests (all dialog-stack invariants)
- test_every_dialog_kind_opens_and_closes_clean -- 2 violations
- test_event_firing_over_each_open_dialog_kind -- 3
- test_opening_each_dialog_kind_over_a_live_event_dialog -- 15
- test_same_frame_collision_event_then_ledger -- 3
- test_rapid_double_open_same_kind -- 2
- test_monkey_full_ops_seeded -- 2 (breaks at step 12)

## Reading
These look like REAL invariant violations of the known dual-source-of-truth modal-state class, i.e. the evidence trail for #877 (LIFO modal chokepoint), not test rot. The suite is doing its job; the process gap is that nothing surfaces the red.

## Asks
1. Triage each of the 6 against #877 scope: expected-pending-chokepoint (annotate/xfail with a pointer) vs independent bug (split out).
2. Add a cheap surfacing mechanism so non-blocking-red is seen (e.g. a scheduled summary or a badge/line in the PR pipeline summary), without making the tier blocking.

## Provenance
Found while verifying PR #960's sim-tier red (verdict: pre-existing, identical on main). Related: #886 (the suite), #877 (the fix), #640 (honest CI).

issues.title: fix(release): v0.13.1.json advertises 404 download URLs; align contact address
issues.body:
Two small release-metadata issues surfaced by the pdoom1-website session (lodged at Pip's direction — please comment back with what's already done / in flight).

## 1. Broken download URLs in `v0.13.1.json`

`v0.13.1.json`'s `downloads.windows` and `downloads.linux` point at `PDoom.exe` and `PDoom.x86_64` — both currently **404**. The real release assets are `PDoom-Windows-v0.13.1.zip` and `PDoom-Linux-v0.13.1.zip` (macOS `PDoom.app.zip` resolves fine). Anything consuming that JSON — an updater, a mirror, a launcher — breaks for Windows/Linux. Reconcile the JSON to the actual asset names, or rename the assets to match the JSON.

_The website itself is unaffected — it reads the live release asset list, not this JSON — but the metadata is internally inconsistent._

## 2. Contact address split

The v0.13.1 release body tells users to email `pip@beacongcr.org`; the entire website uses `team@pdoom1.com`. Pick one canonical address (or emit it as a field consumers can read) so feedback doesn't scatter across two inboxes.

---
_Filed as cross-repo work at Pip's direction (contact-protocol override, 2026-07-27)._

issues.title: feat(engine): integrate frontier-labs dataset (pdoom-data#37); expose a list the website can pull to fix calculate-game-stats
issues.body:
## Ask (follow-on from pdoom-data#37)

Once pdoom-data ships its first-pass frontier-labs dataset (**PipFoweraker/pdoom-data#37** — foundation dates 2000→present), build the follow-on:

1. **Integrate** the frontier-labs list + foundation dates into the game engine (labs as timeline entities that come into existence on their founding dates).
2. **As soon as the MVP is enough for the website to consume it**, expose it so pdoom1-website can pull the list — so we can retire the hardcoded lab list in `calculate-game-stats.py` and drive `frontier_labs_count` (and future stats) from real data.

## Why

pdoom1-website currently hardcodes the frontier-labs list in `scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` to produce a stubbed count. Per the cross-repo protocol (game/data own truth; the website derives), that count should come from the canonical dataset. This also feeds the website's planned "state of doom" stats page.

## Sequencing (please don't block the website on full engine work)

`pdoom-data#37` → **engine integration** → **expose a consumable artifact**. The website does **not** need the full engine integration — it just needs a **stable, fetchable list** of `{id, name, founded, status}`. Please ship that consumable early (a served JSON, or simply point us at the pdoom-data serveable if that's cleaner) even if the richer engine timeline mechanics land later.

## Definition of done (for the website's needs)

- A documented, fetchable artifact of frontier labs + foundation dates.
- The URL + shape noted in a comment here so the pdoom1-website session can wire `calculate-game-stats.py` to it.

---
_Depends on pdoom-data#37. Filed as cross-repo work at Pip's direction (contact-protocol override, 2026-07-27) by the pdoom1-website session._

issues.title: design(hiring): W3 -- revisit the candidate pool cap (MAX_CANDIDATES=6); stale once networking changes, and cap-hits are partly silent
issues.body:
Pip ruling (2026-07-26): the candidate pool cap needs revisiting in W3 if not before -- the cap may be stale as the way networking/sourcing works changes.

## Current state: MAX_CANDIDATES = 6, and it bites in several places

- `game_state.gd:104` -- `const MAX_CANDIDATES: int = 6`, hardcoded (NOT Balance-sourced, unlike most hiring tunables).
- `game_state.gd:597 add_candidate` -- **silently drops** the candidate when the pool is full. No log, no event.
- `hiring_pipeline.gd:186 _add_sourced_candidate` -- returns false at cap. The connections path emits a `connection_pool_full` event (hiring_pipeline.gd:719), but the ADVERTISE path just skips the `advertise_hit` event: **paid campaign candidates are silently discarded at cap**. This is the same failure mode that got the old free per-turn refill removed (see the NOTE at the top of turn_manager.gd) -- sourcing spend competing with a tiny fixed pool.
- `turn_manager.gd _restore_stranded_hires` (PR #960) -- a stranded hire returning to a FULL pool "takes another offer" (visible, but still a loss driven by the cap).
- `hiring_panel_controller.gd:120` -- UI header renders `CANDIDATE POOL (n/6)`.

## Questions for W3

- Is a fixed cap even the right shape once networking changes, or should pool size scale with something (reputation, org size, sourcing investment, an upgrade)?
- If a cap stays: what happens at cap must NEVER be silent -- displacement (worst candidate leaves), refusal-with-message, or a queue, but not a silent drop.
- First step regardless of the design ruling: move the constant to Balance (`hiring.pool_cap` or similar) so it is tunable data, not a const.

Related: #830 (hiring statefulness), #833 (people-and-money cohesion spine), #954 (full candidate cards -- a bigger pool changes that UI's scale assumptions).

issues.title: bug(hiring): queued hire that fails at execution strands the candidate -- vanishes from pool AND queue forever
issues.body:
## Origin (funny)

Filed 2026-07-26 as "28 people ballooning mid-run" from Pip's playtest note "28 visitors, something weird is happening." That turned out to be **28 WEBSITE visitors** (traffic, and good news), not a game bug. The original premise is dead -- but the code archaeology it triggered surfaced a real, verified candidate-leak path, so this issue is repurposed for that.

## The real bug: queued hires can strand candidates (they vanish from the game)

Flow:

1. Player hires a named candidate: `game_manager.gd:251 queue_candidate_hire` appends the Researcher to `state.pending_hire_queue` and **removes them from `candidate_pool` immediately** (double-hire guard).
2. At end-of-turn execution, `actions.gd:231` checks `state.can_afford(execution_costs)` and returns failure **before** the `hire_*_researcher` match arm ever calls `_hire_from_pool`.
3. On that failure path the queued candidate is **never popped from `pending_hire_queue` and never restored to the pool**. Nothing else drains stale queue entries -- the only clears are new-game reset (`game_state.gd:265`) and save-load overwrite (`game_state.gd:1163`, which faithfully round-trips the stranded entry).

Result: if cash drops between queuing and execution (earlier action in the same turn's execution order, an event, payroll), the candidate silently disappears -- not in the pool, not employed, carried forever in a queue no one reads. Player-visible symptom: "I hired someone and they never showed up, and they're gone from the pool."

Secondary path (unverified, lower priority): `actions.gd:679-689` `_hire_from_pool` only dequeues a spec-MATCHING candidate; the normal UI derives the action id from the candidate's own spec so a mismatch should be unreachable today, but the fallthrough silently hires a different pool candidate if it ever happens. Worth an assert.

## Fix sketch

- On the affordability-failure path (and any failure between queue and hire), return the queued candidate to `candidate_pool` (respecting `MAX_CANDIDATES`; if full, at minimum log + drop visibly).
- Or: drain `pending_hire_queue` at end of turn execution -- anyone still queued goes back to the pool with a log line.
- Guard test: queue a hire, force cash below execution cost, end turn, assert candidate is back in the pool and queue is empty.
